body.x: Shawn G. DuBravac, the Chief Economist and Director of Research for the Consumer Electronics Association (CEA), gave a speech on this year's trends to watch at CES 2015, which will run Jan. 6-9 in Las Vegas.
In his presentation, DuBravac said digitization of our physical space, permeation of logic, internet of me, and fragmented innovation are the four trends to watch in 2015.

He also said the five pillars of our digital destiny are as follows: ubiquitous computing, cheap digital storage, connectivity, proliferation of digital devices, and sensorization of tech. And, the emerging technologies are making these five pillars stand up.

He then continued with the big questions for innovation in 2015 are as follows: what to digitize next, how to provide connectivity, where to embed & deploy sensors, and what is the use-case scenario adaptive customization.

Speaking of trend, the U.S. Consumer Electronics Sales and Forecasts predicted that further development of the new devices created with the emerging technology will bring some of the most drastic boom in the electronic market this year.

First of all, there will be a "device revolution" in wearables. The sale of smart watches is expected to jump a whopping 474% from last year, selling 11 million units to generate $3.1 billion in revenue. Advanced technology in smart eyewear will bring in more demand, with an expected sales of 125,000 units, resulting in $181 million in revenue. Twenty million units of fitness and activity trackers are expected to be sold, surpassing $1.8 billion in revenue in 2015.

Drones and 3D printers will be the devices that are expected to make drastic changes to the way we live. 341,000 units Drones is expected to sell, up 49% resulting in $102.8 million in revenue. 30 printers is expected to generate $91 million in revenue.
There will be more sales of smart thermostats, generating $282 million in revenue.

In terms of sales, the leaders of consumer electronics are smartphones and tablets. Though the market for smartphones are already saturated, the sales is still expected to increase 5% to $51.3 billion. Tablets are expected to roll in $24.5 billion in revenue by selling 79.6 million units.

Cars will become smarter with the installation of connected devices to the cars. Though the demand is rising slowly at only 3.3%, automotive electronics is still an attractive market, generating $14 billion.

The electronics that comes in third in sales is 4K ultra HD TV with the revenue of $4.9 billion. However, the demand is expected to increase 106%, more than double from last year. LCD flat panels will be generating $17.4 billion in revenue.

Held annually in January and owned and produced by the Consumer Electronics Association (CEA), CES 2015 is the world's largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition to see the latest global trends in consumer electronics industry in one spot.

Globally recognized for its record in the number of published articles for CES, AVING News has been sending its reporters to CES every year to deliver the fastest and freshest news on the spot. This year, AVING News is using smartphones for news reporting, in line with the trend of one-person media.
